The author is using the term **mouth** to mean “end” or “side.” If this term does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. x.ASV: And he said unto him that was over the vestry, Bring forth vestments for all the worshippers of Baal. And he brought them forth vestments.

nt: In this context, the word **vestment** refers to a special ceremonial garment that priests and worshipers of Baal wore during religious rituals. These garments signified devotion to Baal and added solemnity to the rituals. If your readers would not be familiar with this type of **vestment**, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the ceremonial garment that signified devotion to Baal]

וְ⁠יֵה֞וּא שָׂם־ל֤⁠וֹ בַ⁠חוּץ֙ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ וַ⁠יֹּ֗אמֶר הָ⁠אִ֤ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּלֵט֙ מִן־הָ⁠אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא עַל־יְדֵי⁠כֶ֔ם נַפְשׁ֖⁠וֹ תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֽׁ⁠וֹ

The author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Jehu was using **his life in place of his life** as a common expression of his culture to mean that any of the men he was stationing outside would forfeit his own life if he allowed any of the **men** from inside the temple to escape. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in [1 Kings 20:39](../1ki/20/39.md). Alternate translation: [the one of you who lets him escape will pay for that with his life] or [we will execute the one of you who lets him get away]

x.YLT: And it cometh to pass at his finishing to make the burnt-offering, that Jehu saith to the runners, and to the captains, `Go in, smite them, let none come out;' and they smite them by the mouth of the sword, and the runners and the captains cast them out; and they go unto the city, to the house of Baal,

nt: The author is using the phrase **And it happened** to introduce a new development in this event. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new development.

The term **runners** originally described men who were royal bodyguards and who ran in front of and alongside the king’s chariot to protect him. The term later also described palace guards, as [1 Kings 14:27–28](../1ki/14/27.md) shows. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the term there. Alternate translation: [to the royal guards] or [to the palace guards]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:23](../03/23.md). Alternate translation: [kill them]

The author is using as a common expression of his culture to mean that the runners and captains completely destroyed the worshipers of Baal, leaving no survivors. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in [1 Samuel 22:19](../1sa/22/19.md). Alternate translation: [And they destroyed them completely]

This could mean: (1) that the runners and captains **threw** the dead bodies of the Baal worshipers out of the temple. Alternate translation: [and the runners and the captains threw their bodies out of the temple] or (2) that the runners and captains **threw** the bodies of the people they killed to one side so that they could continue going through the crowd and killing others. Alternate translation: [and the runners and captains threw to one side the body of each person they killed until they had killed everyone]

In this context, the term **city** seems to describe an inner sanctuary of the temple of Baal where the sacred “pillars” described in the next verse were kept. Alternate translation: [the inner sanctuary of the temple of Baal]

Alternate translation: [four generations of your descendants]

Here, sitting on the **throne of Israel** represents ruling Israel as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [will succeed you as the king of Israel]

nt: The author is describing the location of a place in the way that is characteristic of his culture. He means here that if someone were traveling from the territories he is about to describe to the area where most of the Israelites lived, he would be coming **from the rising of the sun**, that is, from the east. In your translation, express this in the way your culture describes the location of places. If you have already translated the book of Joshua, see how you translated the similar expression in [Joshua 12:1](../jos/12/01.md). Alternate translation: [to the east of the Jordan River]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the land of the Gadite and the Reubenite and the Manassite]

The author is not referring to a specific **Gadite**, **Reubenite**, or **Manassite**. He means members of those tribes in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gadites and the Reubenites and the Manassites]

The author means that in addition to capturing **Aroer**, Hazael conquered territory throughout Gilead all the way to **Bashan**. If that is not clear, you may want to use different connecting words to show how the phrase **and Gilead and Bashan** relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [and throughout Gilead all the way to Bashan]
